canberra.title: Wagga greyhound killed after breaking front legs, sparking cover-up accusations
canberra.snippet: A greyhound welfare group has accused Greyhound Racing NSW (GRNSW) of covering up the severity of a racing incident in which a two-year-o...
canberra.content:
Tiggerlong Socks (third) fell over badly after making contact with another dog. Photo: Supplied.

A greyhound welfare group has accused Greyhound Racing NSW (GRNSW) of covering up the severity of a racing incident in which a two-year-old black female dog was euthanised after breaking both front legs at Wagga on Tuesday night (18 August).

Tiggerlong Socks was leading race 11 when she made contact with another dog, Call Me Snuggles, on the first turn.

Tiggerlong Socks fell badly and crashed out of the race.

According to the stewards’ report, an on-track veterinarian examined the dog and found she had compound fractures to her front legs.

A compound fracture means a broken bone has pierced the skin.

The veterinarian euthanised Tiggerlong Socks because of the severity of her injuries.

“Strip away the spin and this is what happened: Tiggerlong Socks was seriously injured while racing at Wagga and was killed because her injuries were so severe she could not be treated,” NSW Animal Justice Party MP Emma Hurst said.

“That should horrify people in NSW in the same way such announcements about the killing of dogs horrified people in other countries that went on to ban greyhound racing such as Wales, New Zealand and Scotland.”

A replay of the race published on the GRNSW-owned TheDogs.com.au website does not show the fall.

In the video, Tiggerlong Socks disappears from view at about the 29-second mark.

NSW MP Emma Hurst said the Wagga track incident should horrify the public. Photo: Emma Hurst/Facebook.

Kylie Field, NSW director of the Coalition for the Protection of Greyhounds, said the removal of the incident amounted to a cover-up.

“As is their policy, GRNSW has censored the incident from the race video,” she said.

“They have to stop hiding the reality of greyhound racing from the public. All race videos must be unedited and uncensored.

“The industry is all smoke and mirrors.

“Tiggerlong Socks was only two years old when she suffered the unimaginable agony of fractures to both her front legs.”

GRNSW is the organisation set up by the NSW Government to run and develop greyhound racing in the state. It was created under NSW law and receives taxpayer funding.

GRNSW said the industry was committed to improving safety.

“Our condolences go out to the trainer, owners and connections of Tiggerlong Socks,” a GRNSW statement said.

“While such outcomes have reduced by more than 93 per cent since 2017-18, and financial year 2025-26 saw a 43 percent decrease in on-track euthanasia from FY 2024-25, the NSW Greyhound Racing industry remains committed to delivering the highest welfare for its canine athletes.

“As part of the industry’s renewed focus and determination to see ongoing reductions in serious injury rates, it has explored and implemented a range of strategies designed to substantially reduce serious injuries.”

GRNSW also said there had been no on-track euthanasia at Wagga in the past 22 months and that Tuesday’s death was the first in that time and only the third in more than three years.

Ms Hurst is not convinced.

“You cannot announce that yet another greyhound has been killed following a racing injury and, in the same breath, boast that you are becoming a ‘world leader in racing safety’. It is absolutely devastating that yet another dog has been killed as part of a pastime hobby,” she said.

Ms Field said GRNSW was misleading the public.

“The NSW Government’s Drake Inquiry into greyhound racing found that while on-track deaths had declined, more dogs were dying away from the tracks due to their racing deaths,” she said.

Ms Hurst wants more transparency around greyhound deaths and injuries.

“The public should be given the full veterinary assessment, the race footage showing the dog’s injury, the nature and severity of her injuries and the circumstances surrounding the decision to kill her. The reality is that the industry has never and probably never will be this transparent because putting a face and a name to yet another victim of this industry isn’t considered good PR,” she said.

“Every dog killed in this industry should come with the same question directed to GRNSW – how many dead dogs does the industry consider acceptable, and how many deaths will it take before this deadly hobby is stopped?”

Original Article published by Oliver Jacques on Region Riverina.

canberra.title: Co-development of high-energy laser opens new opportunities with Japan
canberra.snippet: Australia and Japan have successfully tested a jointly-developed high-energy laser as part of a deepening of defence collaboration betwee...
canberra.content:
Defence Minister Richard Marles and Japan Minister of Defense Koizumi Shinjiro in Canberra on Tuesday (18 August). Photo: Kym Smith via ADV.

Australia and Japan have successfully tested a jointly-developed high-energy laser as part of a deepening of defence collaboration between the two countries.

The milestone comes after Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and his Japanese counterpart Sanae Takaichi announced during their May summit in Canberra a commitment to enhanced defence and security cooperation.

The Boobook project as it has been dubbed is a collaboration between Australia’s Defence Science and Technology Group (DSTG), Mitsubishi Electric Australia (MEA), and Mitsubishi Electric Corporation (MELCO), and has culminated in the successful field testing of the prototype laser system.

The project draws on more than 20 years of research and development by DSTG to deliver the laser technology which also has the potential to enhance surveillance capability.

The successful trials were conducted at the Cultana Training Area in South Australia and at DSTG’s Edinburgh facilities, and gave valuable insights into the system’s design and technical requirements. These insights will inform the next phases of development and commercialisation.

The tests also demonstrated Australia and Japan’s ability to jointly develop advanced technologies and conduct multinational testing on Australian ranges.

As the project progresses, MEA is establishing a new $70 million facility at Rydalmere in Sydney where large-scale manufacturing will be conducted. The facility will be home to a new MEA Defence Division, and will support manufacturing opportunities in Australia and strengthening access to advanced Mitsubishi Electric defence technologies for the Australian Defence Force.

Minister for Defence Industry Pat Conroy said the project demonstrated Australia’s ability to closely collaborate with Japan to develop cutting-edge technologies.

“Boobook is more than a technology project,” he said. “It is a practical example of the growing defence industrial partnership between Australia and Japan, as well as the opportunities that partnership creates for both nations.

“The establishment of Mitsubishi Electric Australia’s new defence facilities in Rydalmere is a strong vote of confidence in Australia’s defence industrial future and will support new opportunities for advanced manufacturing, technology transfer and workforce growth.”

The announcement coincides with the visit to Australia by Japanese Minister of Defense Koizumi Shinjiro, who had his fourth meeting with Defence Minister Richard Marles on Tuesday (18 August) under the bilateral Framework for Strategic Defence Coordination which was established in December 2025.

“I think this is the fourth time we’ve met this year, seventh time we’ve met within a year, and it speaks to the significance of the relationship that we have together, personally, but obviously also in terms of the bilateral defence relationship of our two countries,” Mr Marles said in a statement.

“We meet at a time where there is significant strategic challenge around the world, but very much in the Indo-Pacific. And in the midst of all of that, our relationship is so profoundly important, and we are deeply grateful for it.”

Mr Koizumi added, “The leaders’ statement on security cooperation issued following the Japan-Australia summit meeting in May this year reflects the unprecedented level of strategic alignment between our two countries and will elevate our defence partnership to new heights.”

During their meeting, the two defence ministers committed to advance information sharing between the two defence forces, and to increase the tempo of military exercises. Australia and Japan are increasingly operating a number of similar capabilities, most notably the F-35A Lightning II fighter, and the forthcoming Mogami-class frigate being built for the Royal Australian Navy (RAN).

On the Mogami-class, the ministers said the project was on track to deliver the first of 11 vessels to the RAN by 2030, just five years after the decision was taken to acquire the vessel.

“We remain on course to see the first of those vessels in service in the Royal Australian Navy this decade, making it one of the fastest acquisitions of a surface combatant into the Royal Australian Navy in our history,” Mr Marles said.

“And we could not be happier with the level of cooperation that we are having with the Japanese Government in respect of that, but also the level of cooperation that we are having with [shipbuilder] Mitsubishi Heavy Industries.”

Original Article published by Andrew McLaughlin on PS News.

canberra.title: Bestiality trial ends with Canberra man found guilty of abusing cat
canberra.snippet: CONTENT WARNING: This article contains distressing content and animal abuse. At the end of an unusual and “intense” trial hel...
canberra.content:
A man, aged in his late 20s, faced a charge of bestiality in an ACT Supreme Court trial. Photo: Michelle Kroll.

CONTENT WARNING: This article contains distressing content and animal abuse.

At the end of an unusual and “intense” trial held in Canberra’s courts, a man was found guilty of committing bestiality on a cat.

The man, who is aged in his late 20s but is not named for legal reasons, was alleged to have abused his housemate’s cat, whose name is Dutch, at their home in Canberra in February 2025.

His ACT Supreme Court trial lasted about a day and a half before the lawyers gave their closing addresses.

Jurors deliberated for several hours on Wednesday (19 August) before returning to the courtroom and announcing they had found him guilty of one count of bestiality.

The man, who is in custody, did not visibly react to the verdict.

Afterwards, Chief Justice Lucy McCallum thanked the jurors, saying “the trial was short, but it was intense”.

She adjourned the matter to next month. Sentencing will take place at a future date.

During the trial, the jury heard the man and his housemate went out drinking that night, before the man was the first to return home.

When the housemate came back, he found the man at the kitchen sink, tending to some injuries. The man told him Dutch had attacked him, but when the housemate challenged him on this account, the man broke down.

The housemate told the jury Dutch was normally playful, confident and “a bit of a rascal”. But after he returned home that night, the cat was crouching low, hissed at him and was “really, really pissed off”.

Two veterinarians examined Dutch and reported the injuries on his anus were likely caused by penetration.

Prosecutor Sam McLaughlin said that when the man and the housemate left home that evening, neither Dutch nor the man had any injuries, and that Dutch, a strictly indoor cat, was left inside.

He also said photos showed multiple significant scratches to the man’s hands and arms.

But the man’s barrister, Edward Chen, said DNA test results showed there had been no human DNA inside Dutch’s rectum.

“This point in itself outweighs all the other evidence,” he said.

Mr Chen said an alternative hypothesis was that “something traumatic” happened to Dutch after his client and the housemate had gone out drinking that night.

He said his client returned home first, and perhaps there had been some kind of interaction that caused Dutch to attack him, as the cat was already frightened and in a heightened state.

canberra.title: COVID fraudster’s flood of lies defrauded Services Australia of $18,000
canberra.snippet: A repeat liar spent about a year fraudulently claiming nearly $18,000 from Services Australia in COVID or disaster support payments. A re...
canberra.content:
19 August 2026

Gregory Leonardi, 40, was handed a jail sentence after he repeatedly defrauded Services Australia. Photo: Michelle Kroll.

A repeat liar spent about a year fraudulently claiming nearly $18,000 from Services Australia in COVID or disaster support payments.

A recently-published decision from the ACT Supreme Court revealed 40-year-old Gregory Leonardi was sent to jail for his crimes before he lost an attempt to appeal his sentence.

For nine months, he engaged in a “sustained and deliberate fraud of Services Australia” by falsely claiming financial assistance to which he was not entitled, the court’s Acting Justice Ann Ainslie-Wallace said.

She said he made 49 fraudulent claims mostly under his own name, although he also made claims using other people’s names five times.

In total, he obtained $17,970 in COVID-19 Disaster Payments, Pandemic Leave Disaster Payments, an Australian Government Disaster Recovery Payment and a National Health Emergency Crisis Payment.

“In some, [he] claimed and received payments designed to assist people who were unable to work and earn because of the COVID-19 lockdowns,” Acting Justice Ainslie-Wallace said.

“He sought and obtained payment designed to assist people who were in financial hardship and could not earn because they had to self-isolate.”

Leonardi had been employed full-time and never lost any work shifts due to COVID restrictions or lockdowns.

When he made a claim for the Disaster Recovery Payment, which was supposed to help people adversely affected by a disaster, he lied about living in Braidwood, NSW as well about how his house had been damaged by major flooding.

Leonardi pleaded guilty to three counts of obtaining a financial advantage by deception before the ACT Magistrates Court sentenced him to one year’s jail in July 2026, although he was to be released after spending six months behind bars.

He appealed his sentence, in part arguing it was manifestly excessive and the sentencing magistrate, Magistrate Ian Temby, hadn’t give weight to his subjective circumstances.

But earlier this month, Acting Justice Ainslie-Wallace said his lawyers had not established any errors with his sentence and dismissed his appeal.

For instance, she noted how Magistrate Temby accepted Leonardi was suffering from mental health issues at the time, but not so much that it reduced his moral culpability.

Leonardi will be released from custody in January 2027. He must be of good behaviour for 18 months and repay almost $17,000 to the Commonwealth Government.

canberra.title: ‘My heart goes out to the family’: Kippax butcher saves sleeping family from house fire in Dunlop
canberra.snippet: A Kippax butcher has saved the lives of a family in Dunlop after their garage caught fire on Wednesday morning (19 August). Tom Freeman w...
canberra.content:
Kippax Butcher Tom Freeman saved a Dunlop family from a house fire on Wednesday morning by breaking down the front door and waking up the unsuspecting residents inside. Photos: Jarryd Rowley.

A Kippax butcher has saved the lives of a family in Dunlop after their garage caught fire on Wednesday morning (19 August).

Tom Freeman was preparing for work as usual, waking up at 5 am, defrosting his car’s windscreen, and kissing his wife goodbye.

Unlike every other morning, however, Tom noticed a smell from around the neighbourhood at around 5:45 am that he wasn’t familiar with: the scent of plastic burning.

Despite taking the same route to work every day, Tom decided to do a lap of his street to make sure everything was okay.

What followed was an incredible act of bravery.

“I just went for a little bit of a drive around just to make sure everything was all right, and I saw black smoke billowing out of this person’s garage door,” he said.

“I pretty much just parked the car up real quick, jumped out, grabbed my phone just in case I needed to call the firies, which I did have to after I got the residents out.

“I bashed their door to pieces and pulled the door out of its hinge almost. If that wasn’t going to work, I was going to break their window because I could see what was happening in the garage.”

Upon entering the house, Tom quickly found the people living inside who were still asleep and unaware that the fire had engulfed their garage and was spreading to their home.

“They had no idea why some crazy man was just bashing their door in. They were justifiably terrified,” he said.

“I let them know what was going on, and then the residents came out, and the man occupying the house came out and lifted his garage door up, but it was well and truly alight by that stage.”

Tom rushed to alert the neighbours on either side, making sure they knew about the fire and were prepared in case it spread.

He also called the fire brigade and waited until they arrived before leaving the scene.

Despite his bravery, Tom’s only focus was and still is the family who were affected.

“My heart goes out to the family that’s probably lost more than what I can imagine,” he said.

“I’m not too sure what condition the entire house is in, but from when I left the scene, just before the fire crews got there, it looked pretty devastating.

“I don’t want to be hailed as a hero. I believe that Canberra is full of people who would have done exactly what I did.”

Photos: Jarryd Rowley.

Tom clocked on at work not 20 minutes after leaving the fire.

Still rattled, Tom said he is thankful for his coworkers at Elite Meats who have helped him through a chaotic start to the day.

“If I wasn’t with the boys that I’m with right now, I suppose a bit too much of a deep reflection might happen. Thankfully, I can get stuck into work and take my mind off it,” he said.

“I feel for the family, who very well might have lost everything, but I guess materials can be replaced.

“Right now, I’m just thankful that everyone got out of that situation with their lives.”

australia.content:
ADF joins search for missing 18-year-old bushwalker

Australian defence force personnel have joined the search for 18-year-old Lily Hooper, who has been missing in Nattai national park in the southern highlands for a week.

Hooper was last seen leaving a home on Burragorang Road in Oakdale at about 8am last Wednesday to go hiking. Her family reported her missing after she failed to return home by 10pm.

Her car was found near the Bonnum Pic walking trail in the national park at about 11pm that night.

About 200 emergency services and defence personnel are continuing air and land searches across the area, using specialist crews, trail bikes, horses, dogs and helicopters.

Hooper is described as being of Caucasian appearance, about 175 centimetres tall, with a slim build, long blonde hair and blue eyes. She was last seen wearing a shirt and shorts.

Jewish, Muslim dialogue stalled since terror attacks, royal commission hears

An interfaith leader says Jewish and Muslim communities have stopped interacting since terror attacks, AAP reports.

Faith Communities Council of Victoria’s Sandy Kouroupidis gave evidence about work the group did to promote harmony between people of different faiths at a royal commission on antisemitism and social cohesion.

The 14 December 2025 Bondi massacre, and the 7 October 2023 Nova music festival attack in Israel by Hamas, had a huge impact on Victoria’s Jewish community and its relationships with other religious groups, he said.

Interaction between the Muslim and Jewish communities has stopped altogether, Kouroupidis said. He said.

We have two vice-chairs; one of them is the chair of the Islamic Council of Victoria and the other one is the chair of the Jewish Community Council of Victoria.

It has been very, very challenging to get those two communities in the same room.

Jewish people had stopped attending interfaith events and schools stopped taking part in visits to Muslim and Christian institutes, Kouroupidis said. He said:

A lot of the Jewish schools simply don’t feel safe.

Tanya Plibersek condemns online misogynistic victim-blaming following AFL sexual assault allegation revelations

The federal social services minister, Tanya Plibersek, has condemned the online misogynistic and victim-blaming commentary after the decision to stand down five Sydney Swans players over a breach of standards linked to an investigation into an allegation of sexual assault.

Following the news, social media platforms were flooded with abuse targeting women who came forward.

Speaking on ABC’s Afternoon Briefing, Plibersek said:

It’s disgusting, and isn’t this just one of the reasons so few women come forward?

One of the reasons people don’t come forward is exactly the sort of social media backlash we’ve seen today, with shocking instances of misogyny and victim-blaming. It is incredibly disappointing and that’s when our institutions need to stand up the most.

No arrests or charges have been laid in connection with the allegation.

Tanya Plibersek welcomes AFL player bans after links to sexual assault allegation investigation

The federal social services minister, Tanya Plibersek, has welcomed the Sydney Swans’ decision to ban five players for “serious breach” of standards over an incident that has been linked to an allegation of sexual assault.

No arrests or charges have been laid in connection with the allegation.

Speaking on ABC’s Afternoon Briefing, she called on the AFL to recognise that it “plays an important role in our community” as an organisation that “boys and young men look up to”.

I’m really pleased to hear about some of the measures the club has taken today.

It is important to show that sporting clubs, schools and other institutions take allegations of sexual assault seriously.

It is really important that, in any response, we centre victims and survivors of sexual assault. Hearing the club take strong measures is a really important step forward.

Luca Ittimani

Financial victims to receive less compensation under Labor reforms, Choice says

Victims of financial institutions’ failures are set to receive smaller payouts under government reforms to a compensation scheme, a consumer group has warned.

The assistant treasurer, Daniel Mulino, outlined the reforms to the compensation scheme of last resort (CSLR) today as part of Labor’s response to the collapses of investment funds Shield and First Guardian.

The CSLR will now only pay out on consumers’ actual losses, rather than expected losses. The scheme is funded by certain types of companies working in lending and financial advice but has grown more expensive. Australians with self-managed super funds could also have to start paying levies to fund the scheme.

The Australian Banking Association welcomed the reform, with its chief executive, Simon Birmingham, urging all politicians to support the reforms to “reduce costs across the financial industry”.

Consumer group Choice says the changes will “water down” the CSLR and Treasury had not explained how badly the reforms could cost victims. Head of policy Morgan Campbell said:

The cost of the CSLR for the financial advice industry is so high because there is so much more misconduct in the sector than anyone thought when the scheme was set up. The financial advice industry should be focused on cleaning itself up, rather than pressing the government to water down the compensation available to victims.

Travel subsidies announced for families hit by Victoria Pass closure

The NSW government has extended financial support to Blue Mountains families facing lengthy school commutes, backdating school drive subsidies to the start of the Victoria Pass closure in March.

Eligible students living in Hartley, Little Hartley, Hartley Vale, Kanimbla and Oberon can claim the subsidy. The most recent rate is $0.75 per km for travel by car.

Guardian Australia recently spoke with parents from Little Hartley, including Edwina McCarron, who spends hours each school day driving her two children to access a more direct bus route:

We didn’t move to Hartley with the assumption that it’s an isolated area … we moved 20 minutes from our kids’ school.

The new support also commits to “further improvements to school bus services which have been in place since term 3 commenced”.

A Hartley Families Network survey shows average commute times have surged by two to three hours, with spokesperson Steve McCammon citing a significant impact on family wellbeing. The group is lobbying authorities to allow school buses on to a restricted local-access road, requiring joint approval from Transport NSW, and the Lithgow and Blue Mountains councils.

$100m federal funding boost for Blue Mountains highway

The federal government has committed $100m to the Great Western Highway, funding an extra eastbound climbing lane for the link between the Blue Mountains and central west.

The NSW roads minister, Jenny Aitchison, said widening the road will allow motorists “to safely overtake slower-moving vehicles and trucks”.

Victoria Pass has been closed since March, redirecting drivers on to dangerous detours and sometimes adding hours to regular commutes. A replacement structure over the collapsing, 194-year-old Mitchells Causeway is predicted to open between April and June 2026, with the state government having already committed $100m from its 2026-27 budget.

The NSW shadow regional transport minister, Paul Toole, welcomed the federal announcement but said there is a “lack of business support”:

Promises of round-the-clock work mean nothing to these communities, they need and deserve an accurate opening date.

Affected businesses reporting a 40% loss can access grants of up to $25,000. In late June, an additional $20m in financial support was revealed to increase small business grants in some areas to $25,000.
